Far Side Virtual cover art

James Ferraro’s 2011 cover: an iPad showing a cloud-sky face, pasted over a grainy New York street full of taxis.

Source
Wikipedia: Far Side Virtual
Creator
James Ferraro
Made
October 25, 2011 (Hippos in Tanks)
Style
Vaporwave (precursor; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Uncanny, ironic, consumerist

Inspected the 2000 × 1995 front cover of the Hippos in Tanks digital release in the Cover Art Archive, in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Wikipedia: Far Side Virtual “drew primarily on ‘the grainy and bombastic beeps’ of then-recent past media, such as Skype, Second Life, Windows XP and the Nintendo Wii,” and the utopian virtual offshoot it began “later became associated with the Frutiger Aero Internet aesthetic.” Wikipedia: Vaporwave. See Frutiger Aero.

Observed

  • A black tablet, tilted, fills the left half; its screen shows a face cut out of a blue sky with white clouds, with brush-stroke eyebrows and a red oval mouth.
  • The background is a Manhattan street with yellow taxis, overlaid with heavy colour noise.
  • A small copy of the same tablet sits at the upper right; smeared rainbow shapes and a blurred green-and-red blob float at the edges.
  • The title FARSIDEVIRTUAL runs along the bottom in widely spaced capitals, each letter a different primary colour.

Why it belongs

It shows the style’s irony toward consumer technology before the palette settled. The widely spaced title already anticipates the fullwidth-letter habit.
